proofUses.reason: Disjoint encounter boxes are contracted in a finite domain; pruning spanning trees down to boundary terminals makes each encounter box a branch vertex. The boundary count contradicts a positive volume density.

Independent connections in opposite half-spaces produce a backbone vertex with positive probability. Ergodicity gives existence almost surely, uniqueness connects each infinite root to it, and a finite connecting path contains every pivotal edge.

Integrate the finite-torus second inequality first, then pass to the infinite graph and zero field. Positive supercritical density dominates the field-response remainder. The result is integrated and holds at all differentiability points, not a claim of differentiability everywhere.

The tail series and an improper Riemann sum give the Gamma coefficient below exponent one, a logarithm at one, and a finite-mean slope above one. Logarithmic exponents have the separate minimum-with-one rule.
